opportunities: White-space opportunity in Tier-II and Tier-III cities where organized retail penetration remains limited
Emerging segments such as smart mattresses and subscription models create differentiation pathways for innovative players
threats: Environmental Concerns and Regulations - PU foam production faces scrutiny regarding volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions and recyclability challenges; stricter environmental regulations in North America and Europe are increasing compliance costs for manufacturers
Consumer Perceptions of Quality - some buyers still associate poly-foam mattresses with lower quality compared to latex
Direct-to-consumer brands offering 25-50% lower prices than traditional players are forcing established manufacturers to recalibrate pricing strategies and invest in digital capabilities

Industry shows moderate fragmentation with the top five companies (including Sheela Foam/Sleepwell and Kurlon) estimated to command a major market share in 2024, while start-ups like Wakefit and The Sleep Company gain rapid traction through backward integration and data-driven marketing

overview.business_model: The company manufactures PU Foam blocks at its Ambala facility, cuts/processes them into mattresses (Featherfresh, Restivia brands), pillows and cushions, and also sells customised-density PU Foam to third-party manufacturers of furniture, sports products, seat covers, shoes and apparel; products are sold through a pan-India network of 1,300+ dealers rather than owned retail stores, with certain finished products like pillows made on a job-work basis by third parties.

strategy_growth.risk: Our business operations are majorly concentrated in certain geographical regions and any adverse developments affecting our operations in these regions could have a significant impact on our revenue and results of operations.

Such geographical concentration of our business in this region heightens our exposure to adverse developments related to competition, as well as economic and demographic changes in this region, which may adversely affect our business prospects, financial conditions and results of operations.

Further, as we enter into new markets and geographical areas, we are likely to compete with other players, who might have an established presence, and are more familiar with business practices and have stronger relationships with local customers, relevant government authorities, suppliers or are in a stronger financial position than us, all of which may give them a competitive advantage over us.

concerns_observed: 100% of the Rs. 1,371.65 lakhs Net-Proceeds capex (civil construction plus machinery from M/s A S Enterprises and M/s. Suresh Kumar Jindal Contractor) rests only on vendor quotations; no orders have been placed and the objects are not appraised by any bank or financial institution.

PU Foam capacity utilization at the Ambala facility fell to 38% in H1FY26 (not annualised) from 80% in FY25, 78% in FY24 and 81% in FY23, on an unchanged installed capacity of 15,000 TPA, even as the Issue funds capacity-adding machinery at the same site.

Debtor days rose from 58 (FY23) to 225 (H1FY26); trade receivables reached Rs. 2,471.42 lakhs, 65.26% of H1FY26 revenue, versus 26.99% of revenue in FY25; the working-capital gap widened to Rs. 1,847.87 lakhs in H1FY26 from Rs. 1,533.20 lakhs in FY23.

No long-term agreements exist with customers, suppliers or dealers: top-10 customers were 25.10-28.02% of revenue and top-10 suppliers 78.31-88.34% of purchases across FY23-H1FY26, run through a 1,300+-dealer network with no formal dealer agreements.

Outstanding litigation totals Rs. 726.63 lakhs (227.51% of PAT and 46.41% of networth): by/against the Company Rs. 26.50 lakhs / Rs. 200.13 lakhs, and by/against the Promoters Rs. 280.00 lakhs / Rs. 220.00 lakhs.

Unsecured related-party loans of Rs. 643.75 lakhs outstanding as on 30 September 2025, sourced from Promoters, Promoter Group members and entities such as Charming Fashions Private Limited and Aggarwal Comforts Private Limited, carry 0% interest and are repayable on demand.

History of delayed statutory compliance: 19 delayed RoC e-form filings from FY2020-21 to FY2025-26 (MGT-14, PAS-3, CHG-1, ADT-1, DPT-3, INC-27, AOC-4, DIR-12), plus EPF delays of 16 and 4 days, ESIC delays of 4 and 3 days, and TDS return delays of 10, 48 and 64 days.

The entire product range is produced at one leased facility in Ambala, and revenue is concentrated in four states as of H1FY26 - Punjab (21.53%), Uttar Pradesh (23.52%), Haryana (13.47%) and Delhi (10.95%), together about 69% of revenue.

strengths_observed: EBITDA margin expanded from 1.68% (FY23) to 6.01% (FY24), 5.78% (FY25) and 10.74% (H1FY26); PAT margin rose from 0.87% to 8.43% over the same span, with RONW of 40.79%/33.40%/28.74%/20.40% respectively.
Total debt fell from Rs. 1,840.20 lakhs (FY23) to Rs. 921.61 lakhs (FY25) and Rs. 711.95 lakhs (H1FY26), while networth grew from Rs. 170.78 lakhs to Rs. 1,565.75 lakhs over the same period.
No shares held by Promoters are pledged or otherwise encumbered, and the DRHP discloses no defaults or rescheduling of borrowings.
The Ambala facility holds ISO 9001:2015 and BIS Certification No. IS 7933:2022, and its lease was renewed for a 30-year term running 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2055.
Pre-issue capital structure is uncomplicated: only 7 shareholders as of the Draft Prospectus date, no ESOP/ESPS shares ever issued, and no outstanding convertible instruments, warrants or DVRs.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Full-stack vertically integrated manufacturer: sources principal raw materials (TDI, polyols, catalysts, additives) from local and overseas (Hong Kong, Thailand, Singapore) suppliers at monthly-reset prices with 50-70 day supplier credit; manufactures PU Foam in-house via a continuous foaming line (raw-material mixing, foam forming/settling, curing for at least 12 hours, cutting) at its own facility; combines cut foam with spring/rubberised coir and processes into finished mattresses/cushions in-house; certain finished products such as pillows are outsourced on a job-work basis to third-party manufacturers; distributes exclusively through a pan-India dealer network (no owned retail stores) and also sells PU Foam grades directly to third-party manufacturers of furniture, sports products, seat covers, shoes and apparel.
